newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's CVRD sale depends on courts - BNDES.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's CVRD sale depends on courts - BNDES.

text.p: The planned auction of Brazil's Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD) depends on the courts, said Luiz Carlos Mendonca de Barros, head of the National Development Bank (BNDES), which is overseeing the privatization of the mining company.

Mendonca de Barros said Brasilia was trying to keep the sale on track for 1000 local/1300 GMT Tuesday. He said if the government's lawyers failed to overturn a series of injunctions by 1700 local/2000 GMT, the auction might be off.
"If it's not possible, we will have to carry out a postponement," Mendonca de Barros told reporters in Brasilia.
"It will depend on court decisions," he said.
Earlier, BNDES privatization chief Jose Pio Borges said 103 lawsuits had been filed against the sale of the world's largest iron ore exporter, and nine injunctions had been granted.
"The auction is suspended due to court decisions," Borges said in Rio de Janeiro.

Mendonca de Barros, responding to questions about why the the BNDES had not been better prepared to fend off the deluge of legal challenges, said it was impossible for the bank to maintain lawyers in every single town and city.
Forty-five percent of CVRD's voting shares were due to go on the auction block at Rio's stock exchange Tuesday.
But the government Monday failed to overturn one injunction issued in Sao Paulo, and it was unclear how the government would be able to reverse the others in time.
